signaled and unsignalled delays in food presentation, when made contingent on drinking, function as punishers of schedule-induced drinking.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a model for the analysis of schedule-induced drinking.
the effects of events contingent on schedule-induced drinking on the occurrence of drinking and other behavior.
the effects of events dependent on drinking, which are similar in some respects to the effects of events made dependent on other forms of operant behavior.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the schedule-induced drinking is a form of operant behavior, that the drinking is controlled by its consequences, and that the schedule-induced behavior is subject to the same principles as are the other forms of operant behavior.
schedule-induced drinking can be reduced or eliminated when it is followed by a signaled delay in food presentation or when it is followed immediately by an unsignaled delay in food presentation.
schedule-induced drinking in the rat is subject to punishment by both unsignaled and signaled delay of food presentation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the consequences of drinking are more important to the maintenance of drinking than are the consequences of licking.
schedule-induced drinking is not a unitary phenomenon but is subject to the control of its consequences.
schedule-induced drinking is a behavior that is subject to punishment, and the effects of punishment are greater when it is signaled than when it is unsignaled.
The main takeaway from our work is that
schedule-induced behaviors can be influenced by their consequences, and that the effects of consequences can be studied using a variety of experimental techniques.
the consequences of drinking are not always reinforcing.
